CARTA holds Northern Rhône as an analytical corridor between Vienne and Valence whose only mapped extent is the union of the eight separately delimited cru areas. No Northern Rhône boundary exists in law and none is drawn here.

The corridor's spine is described by its appellations rather than mapped by CARTA: Saint-Joseph alone runs roughly sixty kilometres along the right bank. No river centreline geometry is asserted in this release.

Specialist importer sources place Chaillot among the named Cornas sites worked successively by Robert Michel, Noël Verset, Guillaume Gilles and Franck Balthazar. CARTA holds no parcel geometry and does not treat the name as one undivided holding.

The Rare Wine Co. describes La Geynale as a prized sub-cru high on the Reynard slope, planted by Robert Michel's grandfather in 1910; Polaner records vines there passing from Michel to his nephew Vincent Paris. No parcel geometry is asserted.
Reynard is described as a named Cornas slope worked by Robert Michel, Noël Verset and, after Verset sold him early-twentieth-century vines there, Thierry Allemand. No parcel geometry is asserted.

The estate and the Condrieu growers' organisation place the Coteau de Vernon as the site of Francis Vernay's foundational hectare of Viognier and of the terrace reconstruction Christine Vernay completed. No parcel geometry is asserted.

Hervé Souhaut's estate base is at Arlebosc in the northern Ardèche, in the hills above Saint-Joseph and outside that appellation's geography. The base is not the location of the Saint-Joseph vines, and no coordinate is asserted.

Dard & Ribo work from a cellar base at Mercurol while farming rented parcels across Crozes-Hermitage, Hermitage and Saint-Joseph. One base point could not stand for that patchwork even if a coordinate had been acquired; none is asserted here.
